chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, he said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who leads a people in prayer and prays the ʿaṣr prayer, while for them it is the ẓuhr prayer. He said: It sufficed for them, and it sufficed for him.

So this does not conflict with the first report, because the proper way regarding it is that we interpret it as applying to one who does not follow the Imam in the prayer itself and intends ẓuhr for himself; then his prayer is valid even if the Imam is praying ʿaṣr. The first report applies to one who follows his prayer and binds his prayer to it. So if the Imam’s prayer is ʿaṣr, and the one who prayed behind him did not intend ẓuhr for himself, then his ʿaṣr prayer is invalid, because he has not yet prayed ẓuhr, and the ʿaṣr prayer is not valid for one who has not prayed ẓuhr, unless its time has become constrained, as we have explained.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَتْ: was sufficient and fulfilled the obligation

ai.seo_question: Is it valid to pray ẓuhr behind an Imam who is praying ʿaṣr?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal ruling of praying behind an Imam who is performing ʿaṣr while the follower intends ẓuhr. It distinguishes between one who independently intends ẓuhr for himself and one who fully follows the Imam’s prayer as ʿaṣr; the latter is invalid if he has not yet performed ẓuhr, except when the time for ʿaṣr has become too constrained.
